finding: Superimposed pre-eclampsia (SPE) in women with chronic hypertension was associated with increased risk of prematurity and higher rates of neonatal intensive care unit admission compared to those without pre-eclampsia.
mod_finding: Women with chronic hypertension and superimposed pre-eclampsia had a higher incidence of cesarean delivery compared to those without pre-eclampsia (79.64% vs. 62.38%, P=0.003).
birth_weight: Mean birth weight: SPE group - 2577g ± 938, NPE group - 3128g ± 723
